summary.tldr: Requires the government to develop and report on a national housing strategy for Canadians aged 17 to 34.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister to develop a national strategy on housing for young Canadians after consulting provinces, territories, housing groups, municipalities, young Canadians and other stakeholders.
Requires the strategy to assess housing affordability and availability for young Canadians, including rental housing, student housing and entry-level home ownership.

Requires the strategy to include measures to improve access to affordable and secure rental housing, support first-time home buyers, and encourage more rental, student, co-operative and affordable housing.
Requires the strategy to consider existing federal, provincial, territorial and municipal housing plans and to identify ways to reduce barriers for young Canadians.

Requires the Minister to hold at least one conference during the strategy’s development, table the strategy report within 18 months, and table a follow-up report on its effectiveness within four years.
summary.background: The bill defines a young Canadian as a person in Canada who is at least 17 years old but less than 35 years old. It also requires the Minister to be designated by the Governor in Council.
